title: Test kb copies are hard links of a scanned per-session template
goal: conftest.copy_kb and test_stress.copy_kb build each kb copy as hard links of one per-session template whose files were read once, and a session-end check fails the run when any template file changed, so a write through a link cannot pass unnoticed.

gates.question: Hard-linked copies share file content with the template: a test or tool that rewrites a file in place (open(..., 'w')) writes through to the template and to every other copy. Which safety does the story use?
options: hard links plus a session-end digest check of the template, and copies that break the link before a test writes (write through a replace helper)
hard links only for copies no test writes to (the stress suite's read-only base, the tests' read-only kb copies), plain copies elsewhere
no hard links: keep plain copies and accept the first-open cost
gates.recommendation: hard links only for copies no test writes to (the stress suite's read-only base, the tests' read-only kb copies), plain copies elsewhere
gates.answer: hard links only for copies no test writes to (the stress suite's read-only base, the tests' read-only kb copies), plain copies elsewhere

notes: Measured: the first read of a fresh clone's 1,841 files takes 18.9 s and the second 0.3 s; a plain copy's first read 19.4 s, a hard-linked copy's 0.4 s. check.py on a fresh copy takes 15.3 s, on a read one 1.4 s. The stress suite makes about 96 copies per run (88 tests plus 8 per-worker bases). Expected saving: up to 1,600 of stress_test.py's 3,495 worker-seconds, and a similar share of the tests' plain copies. NTFS allows at most 1,023 hard links to one file; a run keeps its passing copies until the session ends (tmp_path_retention_policy failed), so the copy count per run must stay under that. The attribution of the first-open cost to Defender is inferred, not recorded; ST-xjb4wykm “Defender's cost on test scratch files is measured and settled by the operator” records it. Kept as a draft: the operator has not scheduled the test-speed epic EP-hlnsqx4f. Its checks name _tools/perfcheck.py and _tools/test_ids_baseline.txt, which ST-c35i7vjx "A tool proves a test-suite speed-up lost no test" creates, so that story comes first.
